deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematical derivation. It holds two short notes-to-self, separated by horizontal rules.

(1) Continuation of the last line of the previous page: "Studire die [?] Stosskräfte in der Mie-Bornschen Elektrodynamik und überhaupt in der Relativitätstheorie." In English: "Study the [?] impact/collision forces in the Mie–Born electrodynamics and in relativity theory generally." This is a research memo. It concerns how particle collisions (Stoß), and the forces acting in them, could be described within Gustav Mie's nonlinear field theory of matter (1912–13), as reformulated by Max Born (1914) through a Hamiltonian/variational principle. Hilbert's 1915 'Grundlagen der Physik' built directly on this Mie–Born framework. The note fits the surrounding pages: the previous page treats Boltzmann-style most-probable velocity distributions in kinetic gas theory, where collisions are central. So the question is how collision dynamics appears in a relativistic field theory of matter. This suggests a date of roughly 1913–1916.

(2) "Kronecker war inconsequent; er hätte auch die ganze Zahl erst recht verbieten müssen." In English: "Kronecker was inconsistent; he should, a fortiori, have forbidden the integer as well." This is a foundational/philosophical remark. Kronecker banned irrational numbers and completed infinite totalities, accepting only the natural numbers as given ('Die ganzen Zahlen hat der liebe Gott gemacht'). Hilbert objects that the integers themselves (the concept 'ganze Zahl', i.e. the unbounded totality or the general notion of number) already involve the infinite. A consistent restriction would therefore have to exclude them too, and so Kronecker's line is arbitrary.

There are no formulas, computations or steps to reconstruct.

deep.surprise_reason: Both notes match well-documented interests of Hilbert. One is his engagement with Mie–Born electrodynamics around 1913–1916. The other is his repeated published criticism of Kronecker's restrictions on mathematics. The terse 'a fortiori ban the integers' wording is a mildly nice private formulation, but it is not new in substance.
transcription_corrections: The transcription is essentially correct. Line 1 reads 'dynamik und überhaupt in der Relativitäts-' (Hilbert writes the u-umlaut as 'ü'), completing 'Mie-Bornschen Elektro-' from the previous page.
'inconsequent' is Hilbert's own spelling (for 'inkonsequent'); 'müssen' is underlined in the original, with a rule under it.
